# EvidenSe

> EvidenSe is an independent advisory practice based in Lausanne, Switzerland, founded and run by Stéphane Schwander. It helps sport organisations, rights holders, brands and investors understand where commercial value is really being created, and what to grow, fund, back or stop.

## What EvidenSe does

The core thesis: visibility is not durable commercial value. Reach is easy to measure, easy to grow and easy to report. Monetisable demand is none of those things, so organisations optimise what they can see and hope the money follows. EvidenSe closes that gap by turning scattered commercial, audience and sponsorship signals into decisions that survive contact with a board or an investment committee.

The main engagement is the Decision Sprint: a fixed-scope, fixed-fee engagement of three to four weeks that gathers the organisation's commercial, audience, digital and sponsorship data, tests pricing, packaging, rights structure and audience quality, and delivers a board ready recommendation on what to grow, hold, reprice or stop. No retainer, no time-based billing, senior-led throughout.

Three domains of work: Sport Revenue Intelligence (commercial friction audits, asset repackaging, revenue sprints); Predictive Investment and Due Diligence (investment memos, target simulation, portfolio and partnership review); Decision systems for federations (fractional chief strategy support, AI-assisted decision workflows).

Method: modelling and AI process the evidence faster and more systematically than a traditional consulting team can, and are never used to produce the answer. Where predictive modelling genuinely adds value, EvidenSe works with selected partners including Largo.ai, an EPFL spin-off. Modelling processes the evidence. Senior judgement turns it into the decision.

## Who it is for

- Federations and leagues whose audience has grown faster than their revenue
- Investors, funds and acquirers about to commit capital to a sport property, team or sporttech target
- Brands and sponsors being asked to pay for exposure and needing an independent view of what that audience is worth
- Federations and institutional bodies facing a congress, budget cycle or rights renewal where the internal view will not converge

## About the founder

Stéphane Schwander spent nine years at UEFA (2005 to 2014), first as an application specialist on UEFA.com and then as Digital Operations Manager, and eleven years at the FEI, the international federation for equestrian sport, as Commercial Manager, Digital Partnerships (2015 to 2017), Head of Digital (2018 to 2024) and Head of Content and Platform Management (2024 to 2026). At the FEI he built and ran one of the strongest digital operations in Olympic sport, turning the federation into its own media platform: the owned audience grew from 351,000 to 5.3 million; in his final year paid media spend was cut by 78 percent and the audience still grew by 7 percent; 81 percent of video consumption ran through owned channels; a media offer on those channels booked over CHF 1 million in its first ten months; and he founded the FEI Media House, a joint venture with ClipMyHorse.TV. The operation was independently measured for ASOIF in the first quartile of Olympic international federations on owned channels, and won Best Entertainment, Leisure and Travel Campaign at the Alliance of Independent Agencies awards, London 2022. Before UEFA he founded WNG, a web and new media agency in Lausanne, in 2001, and built it to CHF 1.9 million in turnover with a team of nine. More than two decades of international experience across Olympic federations, European football and start-ups. He lectures at Toulouse Business School, has given guest lectures at the Institute of Sport Sciences of the University of Lausanne (UNIL) at the invitation of Professor Markus Lang, mentors start-ups in the TECH4SPORT Accelerator at ThinkSport (the Lausanne-based international sport cluster), sits on ThinkSport's Sport Innovation Challenge Council, and advises start-ups directly, currently as adviser to PickEat.it (https://pickeat.it). LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephaneschwander/

The differentiator: consultants have the models but have never carried a decision through a congress. Federation insiders have the credibility but not the modelling. EvidenSe works in the overlap.

## EvidenSe Sport Attention Index

https://index.evidense.io, its own subdomain: a monthly ranking of public attention across the international federations of the Olympic programme, built from open signals such as Wikipedia readership and search interest, published on the 3rd of each month.

## EvidenSe Labs

Public experiments that test the EvidenSe method in the open (https://www.evidense.io/labs). Each starts from one commercial question, is measured against real data, and stays a working experiment rather than a platform. Each lab's tool runs on its own subdomain; its presentation page lives on www.evidense.io.

- La Sponsoring Machine. Tool: https://sponsoring-machine.evidense.io (behind a login, in French and German). Presentation: https://www.evidense.io/labs/sponsoring-machine (French: https://www.evidense.io/fr/labs/sponsoring-machine, German: https://www.evidense.io/de/labs/sponsoring-machine). An EvidenSe service that helps amateur sports clubs across Switzerland value, structure and sell their sponsorship. In about twenty minutes a club gets an estimate of its sponsorship value (a plausibility range), the gap with what it collects today, three offer tiers and a personalised sponsorship brochure. In the beta, EvidenSe also delivers ten relevant local companies identified from public sources (company websites, the Swiss commercial register Zefix), with the contact person the company publishes and ready-to-send messages the club sends from its own mailbox. The demo is free. The valuation model was tested in 2026 against the real sponsorship income of six clubs in French-speaking Switzerland; two clubs joined the beta. Field research by Jessy Ducommun, as part of his master's thesis at the University of Lausanne (he is also sponsorship manager of LUC Floorball Epalinges). The project was presented to club committees in the Club Management course at Swiss Olympic's Maison du Sport in Ittigen.

Email: hello@evidense.io. Based in Lausanne, working internationally. First step is a thirty minute conversation, no material required in advance.
